step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified Producer compute layers (EC2, Lambda Producer, Fargate) generating logs on the right side.
2. Identified Processor log collection layers (Logstash, Lambda Processor, FluentBit) in the middle column.
3. Identified the centralized search & storage engine (OpenSearch) on the left.
4. Identified access control elements (Users actor and Okta identity provider) providing index filtering and RBAC into OpenSearch.
5. Mapped data ingestion flows from producers through processors into OpenSearch, and access control flows from Users through Okta to OpenSearch.

graph.name: Benevity Centralized Logging Architecture with OpenSearch
graph.notes: Benevity migrated from disjointed log destinations to a centralized OpenSearch architecture, cutting 16 hours/month of maintenance. Logs from EC2, Lambda, and Fargate pass through respective processors (Logstash, Lambda Processor, FluentBit) into OpenSearch, with access governed via Okta.

edges.notes: EC2 logs are pushed to Logstash
Logstash ships processed logs to OpenSearch
Lambda producer sends logs to Lambda log processor
Lambda processor streams logs to OpenSearch
Fargate container logs are sent to FluentBit sidecar via FireLens
FluentBit forwards container logs to OpenSearch
Okta enforces role-based access control and index filtering on OpenSearch
